title: Predicting and questioning while reading
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Predicting and questioning while reading
card: A reader guesses what will happen or be said next, using clues so far such as the title, the headings and what has already happened.
A reader asks questions as they go, such as why a character acted that way or what a word means. Questions keep the reader thinking about the text.
A reader stops now and then to ask whether they still understand. If not, they can reread, read on or look up a word.
A prediction is a guess, so it can turn out to be wrong. A reader then changes the prediction and keeps reading.
draft.remember: Good readers guess ahead, ask questions and stop to check they still understand.

a.q: Sam reads a story in which a boy hears a strange scratching at his window. Sam thinks, "I bet he finds a stray cat." What is Sam doing?
a.why: Sam uses a clue from the story to guess what comes next, which is predicting. It is not checking understanding, because Sam is not testing whether he has followed the text so far.
a.clue: Is Sam guessing ahead or looking back?

b.q: Priya is reading an article about coral reefs. She reaches a paragraph she cannot follow, so she stops and rereads the one before it. What is she doing?
opts: Predicting what the next heading will be
Asking why the writer chose the title
Guessing how the article will end
b.why: Priya notices she is lost and rereads to fix it, which is checking understanding. Rereading might seem like questioning, but she is not asking a question about the text. She is repairing her understanding.
b.clue: She noticed a problem and did something to fix it.
